experiment: E5: linked anchor with a head witness (round 13)

placement.host_a: Home Assistant OS 18.3 (generic-aarch64) in a QEMU/HVF VM on the evaluation Mac; Core run privileged by the Supervisor (as E1)
placement.host_b: Docker Desktop's Linux VM on the same Mac: linked anchor (hpr-anchord:linked), monitor (hpr-monitor:e1), replicator (hpr-e1-replicator:1), and E1's MQTT broker and device simulator
placement.witness: testbed/anchord/headwitness.py as a python3 process on the Mac itself, outside both VMs, bound to 127.0.0.1; the anchor reaches it through host.docker.internal
placement.key_fingerprint_sha256_16: 18041f2da21fe542 (append key; not recorded; held only by the anchor and monitor containers on host B)
placement.witness_key_fingerprint_sha256_16: dbbcc1e330b2abc1 (witness key; not recorded; held only by the anchor container and the witness process on the Mac)

second.what: anchored second-segments inside the run window that no PS trial touched and that fail recomputation

minute.what: anchored minute-segments inside the run window that no PS trial touched and that fail recomputation

link_check.integrity: linked: reordering, deletion and rewriting of records are detectable; a truncated tail or a replaced chain is not, without an externally held head

witness_check.rule: headwitness.py: the latest head is the accepted head with the highest sequence number; the chain must hold at least that many records and its record at that sequence number must have that digest (chainverify.verify_chain with the external head)

against_latest_head.integrity: linked and checked against the externally held head

truncated_tail.what: chain cut to the 224 records before the witness's latest head (seq 225)
problems_against_witness_head: chain holds 224 records but the external head is at 225: truncated or replaced

rewritten_root_unrelinked.what: record 113: root of second-segment 1791428555 replaced, later links left as they were
problems_against_witness_head: prev_digest does not match the previous record

rewritten_root_relinked.what: record 113: root of second-segment 1791428555 replaced and every later prev_digest recomputed (an anchor-host rewrite)
problems_against_witness_head: record does not have the externally held head digest: rewritten or replaced

push_latency.mode: sync (pushed before the append is acknowledged; a failed push never refuses an append)

sync_push_ms_from_anchor_replies.source: the anchor's append replies as the monitor logged them (ticks 1-3 and every twelfth tick, so a sample of the appends)

witness_receipt_minus_anchor_receipt_ms.what: witness_recv_ts (Mac clock) minus anchor_recv_ts (host B clock, taken before the record is written and fsynced), for every accepted head; includes the write, the fsync, the push and the clock offset below

caveats: The monitor container runs hpr-monitor:e1's monitor.py (placement.monitor_in_image_sha256_16); the verifier imports the repository's monitor/monitor.py (code below). They are the same file only if the two hashes agree; otherwise only the commitment code they share bears on the detection result.

Witness receipt minus anchor receipt is taken on two clocks; negative samples show moments when the clocks disagreed by more than the push time, so the single-clock push times in the anchor's replies are the measurement of the push itself.
All three machine contexts (host A's VM, Docker's VM, the Mac) run on one Mac; the witness is outside the anchor host's VM but shares the physical machine and its owner.
Host A's Core can reach the witness's port through the QEMU gateway (probe_from_hub); it holds no witness key, so it cannot push a head.
The links and the witness bind the chain's records; that a first anchored root describes the rows the monitor read still rests on the anchor host being honest when it appends.
